integration_issues.issue: ScrollToHash retry loop finds element and calls scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}) too early — while Landing's lazy images/videos above Gallery are still loading. The smooth-scroll animation locks its target Y at call-time (~scrollY 3718). By the time layout stabilizes, docHeight has grown, Gallery is now at scrollY ~6063, but animation already ended. Result: URL=/#gallery ✅ but element ends at viewport top=2344px (spec requires -50..500). Diagnostic: at t+1500ms scrollY=3718 top=2344; stays at that through t+10000ms. Manual instant scrollIntoView after animation ends lands at top=-0.35 (correct).
Same root cause. scrollY=5055 but #contact.top=4107 (target sits 4107px below viewport). Partially closer to top than gallery but still fails -50..500 requirement.

action_items: Fix ScrollToHash smooth-scroll layout-shift issue in /app/frontend/src/App.js. Recommended fixes (any one): (a) Change behavior from 'smooth' to 'auto' (instant) — no animation, no layout-shift interruption. Diagnostic proves instant scrollIntoView lands perfectly at top=-0.35. (b) After first scrollIntoView, keep re-calling scrollIntoView every 200ms for another 1-1.5s to re-correct once lazy content settles (compensates for docHeight growth). (c) Wait for Landing's below-fold images/videos to load before calling scrollIntoView — e.g., use IntersectionObserver on the target or listen to 'load' events on nearby imgs. Option (a) is simplest and provably works.

Suggested code: replace 'el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "start" });' with either behavior:'auto' OR add a follow-up: setTimeout(() => el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'auto', block:'start'}), 800) after the first call.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js ScrollToHash retry loop is correct in principle, but 'behavior: smooth' interacts badly with lazy-loading landing page — animation target is captured at call-time and cannot follow docHeight growth. Either use instant scroll or add a settling re-scroll.

Landing page renders 6000+ px of content below the fold with lazy images/videos — any hash-anchor navigation needs to account for layout shift AFTER initial mount. Consider adding loading='eager' to critical hero/section images or reserving explicit heights so docHeight stabilizes earlier.
Footer.jsx (verified) — Experiences link now correctly removed; no dead links remain in footer nav.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The retry loop in ScrollToHash IS executing and scrollIntoView IS being called (confirmed via diagnostic: at t+1000ms scrollY jumps from 0 to 153, reaches 3718 at t+1500ms, then flatlines). The problem is behavior:'smooth' snapshotting the animation target early. To retest after fix: on /supper-club/barsaat click [data-testid='nav-gallery'], wait 4s, assert document.getElementById('gallery').getBoundingClientRect().top BETWEEN -50 and 500. Same for #contact from /supper-club/barsaat, and #gallery from /menus. If main agent switches to behavior:'auto' or adds a settling re-scroll, this should pass. The manual instant scrollIntoView at t=10s lands at top=-0.35, proving that as long as the scroll fires AFTER layout settles (or is repeated), the target is reachable.
rca of the issue: Root cause: In /app/frontend/src/App.js ScrollToHash effect, once retry loop finds the element it calls el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'}). Chrome captures the target scroll position (element.top + current scrollY) at that moment and animates towards that Y over ~500-700ms. During those 700ms, Landing's lazy-loaded images/videos ABOVE Gallery finish loading, growing document height from ~9888 to ~10431 px and pushing Gallery down by ~570px. The animation, already locked on the OLD Y, ends short of the new position — leaving the element 2344px below viewport. Reproduction: /supper-club/barsaat → click nav-gallery → wait 4s → getBoundingClientRect().top = 2344 (fail). Mitigation options: (1) use behavior:'auto' (instant) so no animation is interrupted by layout shift — diagnostic manual call confirms this lands at top=-0.35; (2) schedule a second scrollIntoView 800ms after the first to correct residual drift; (3) delay the initial scrollIntoView until all above-target lazy media has loaded (IntersectionObserver / img.complete polling).
